**Retail Performance Dashboard · Aurora Living**

Power BI portfolio project  ·  Sushmita De

# **1\. Project at a glance**

Aurora Living is a fictional Indian home and lifestyle retailer with 20 stores, a website and an app across 5 regions, operating during 2023-2025.

The leadership wants one place to answer following questions:  
**Are we hitting the target?**   
**Where do we lose profit?**   
**Which customers matter most?**   
**Are deliveries and marketing spends working?**   
I built a Power BI report that answers these from 3 years of sales, customer, delivery and marketing data.

| Source Data | 12 raw CSV files (120k orders, ₹1.35bn of net sales) simulated using python, including tables for orders, order lines, shipment details, product and customer details, etc. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **What I built** | Power Query cleaning, a snowflake data model (4 fact tables, 8 dimensions), 40+ DAX measures, 5 report pages plus a drill-through page, and dynamic row-level security |
| **Skills used** | Power BI · Power Query · DAX · data modelling · row-level security · data storytelling |

# **2\. Preparing the Data**

The raw files came with realistic problems. I fixed them all in Power Query, so every fix is a recorded step that reruns on each refresh.

| Problem in the raw data | How I fixed it |
| :---- | :---- |
| Duplicate orders (1.5%) | Remove Duplicates, so sales and orders aren't double-counted |
| Mixed date formats (3% written dd/mm/yyyy) | Change Type with locale English (India), which parses both formats in one step |
| Prices stored as text, e.g. “₹2,939.00” | Removed ₹ and commas, then converted to decimal |
| Negative quantities (0.3%) | Took the absolute value and flagged the row in a qty\_corrected column, so the decision stays visible |
| One value spelt many ways: “north”, “NORTH ”, “North Region”; “Swift Ship”, “SWIFTSHIP” | Trim, Capitalize Each Word and Replace Values, so slicers and joins see one value |
| Blank promotion, return reason and sub-category | A “No Promotion” key (PRM00), “Not Specified” and “Unclassified”, so rows stay visible instead of appearing as (Blank) |

## **Shaping the tables**

* **Merged files that share a grain:** order lines \+ returns became fact\_sales; orders \+ shipments \+ reviews became fact\_fulfilment.  
* **Allocated shipping cost** from each order to its lines by value proportion, so product-level profit is correct.  
* **Built customer lifetime metrics** (first and last order, order count, total spend) that drive the RFM segments and cohorts.  
* **Maintained intermediate queries as staging** with load disabled, so the model holds only the final tables.

# **3\. Data model and DAX**

![Data model diagram: four fact tables (Targets, Sales, Fulfilment, Spend) connected to eight dimension tables, with Date linked to every fact table][image3]

*Snowflake schema: 4 fact tables at their own grain, joined only through shared dimensions. Arrows show filter direction.*

* **Region comes from the customer, not the store**, because online orders have no store region. One security rule on dim\_region then filters all 4 fact tables.  
* **Targets keep their own grain** (month x region x category), so fact\_targets links to Date, Region and Category, not to products.  
* **No fact-to-fact joins**, so filters never take an ambiguous path. Return, delivery and review dates use inactive relationships, switched on with USERELATIONSHIP.

## **DAX highlights**

| Measure | How it works |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Target Revenue** | TREATAS maps monthly targets onto the calendar; the measure returns blank under store, product or promotion filters a target can't respond to. |
| **YoY % and Net Sales LY** | SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR, shown only when one year is selected, so multi-year views never show a misleading comparison. |
| **Repeat rate, segments, retention** | Context transition over customers, ALLSELECTED shares of total, and retention by quarters since first purchase. |
| **Row-level security** | \[manager\_email\] \= USERPRINCIPALNAME() on Dim\_Region, so each regional manager sees only their region (tested with View as). |

# **4\. The dashboard, page by page**

Each page answers one business question. On the 5 analysis pages, every chart has a subtitle that states its finding, an “About this page” box sums up the page, and Year and Region slicers let a manager focus on any year or region.

| ![Overview page of the Aurora Living Power BI report][image6] | Executive Overview Answers: How is the business doing, and is it on target? Shows: KPI cards with year-on-year change, monthly sales vs target, region bars coloured by target status, category and channel mix, and a Top 5 products table that drills through to product detail. |
| :---- | :---- |
| ![Sales vs Targets page of the Aurora Living Power BI report][image7] | **Sales vs Targets Answers:** Where did we miss the target, and why? **Shows:** Cumulative and monthly variance, a category x region heatmap, a 3-year achievement trend by region, and a table that splits growth into orders, customers and order value. |
| ![Profitability page of the Aurora Living Power BI report][image8] | **Profitability Answers:** Where is profit made and lost? **Shows:** A gross-sales-to-profit waterfall, sales vs margin by category (bubble size \= return rate), margin at each discount level, and return reasons with fixable causes in blue. |
| ![Customer Insights page of the Aurora Living Power BI report][image9] | **Customer Insights Answers:** Who are our best customers, and do they come back? **Shows:** New vs returning customers by month, lifetime value by loyalty tier, customer segments by share of customers vs revenue, and a quarterly cohort-retention heatmap. |
| ![Operations & Marketing page of the Aurora Living Power BI report][image10] | **Operations & Marketing Answers:** Are we delivering on time, and is marketing paying back? **Shows:** Monthly on-time delivery, on-time % by carrier and region, average rating by delivery delay, and ROAS vs CAC by acquisition channel. |
| ![Product Details (drill-through) page of the Aurora Living Power BI report][image11] | **Product Details (drill-through) Answers:** How is one product doing against its category? **Shows:** Opened by right-clicking any product: a dynamic title and filter label, margin and return rate against the category average, a monthly trend that adds last year when one year is selected, sales by region and return reasons. |

# **5\. What the analysis found**

Six findings, each with the action it supports. Sales figures are for 2025; the rest cover 2023-25.

| Insights | Recommended actions |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Growth is strong, but the East is slipping.** 2025 net sales grew 20.9% to ₹542M, 4.7% above target. East fell from 110% of target in 2024 to 87%: it gained 24% more customers, but orders fell 6% as they bought less often. | Rebuild repeat buying in East with re-engagement campaigns and loyalty offers |
| **Deep discounts lose money.** Margin falls from 32% at full price to \-6% at 40% off; discounts of 35% or more are loss-making. | Cap promotions below 35% off |
| **Returns cost more than discounts.** Refunds (₹133M) exceed all discounts (₹97M), and 70% of returns have fixable causes, led by transit damage. Furniture sells the most but has the lowest margin (10%) and the highest return rate (18%). | Improve packaging and product descriptions, starting with Furniture |
| **Late deliveries hurt ratings.** Any delay drops the average rating from 4.2 to about 2.5. Parcel Path is on time 68% of the time vs Swift Ship's 92%, and on-time delivery dips to 78% in the Diwali rush. | Shift volume to Swift Ship and add carrier capacity before October |
| **A few customers drive most revenue.** Champions are 16% of customers but 44% of revenue, while 29% of customers are At Risk or Churned. | Protect Champions with loyalty perks; run a win-back campaign for At Risk customers |
| **Marketing efficiency varies 25x.** Email returns 152x its spend at ₹596 per new customer; Influencer returns 6x at ₹7.8K per customer. | Shift budget from Influencer to Email and Affiliate |
